description: Controlled vocabulary defining canonical observable microwave backhaul symptoms recognized by A.R.I.A. Symptoms describe what is observed and shall remain distinct from failure modes, root causes, and diagnoses.

symptom_types.name: LOW_RSL
symptom_types.description: Received Signal Level is materially weaker than the applicable expected, engineered, historical, or threshold value.

symptom_types.name: HIGH_RSL
symptom_types.description: Received Signal Level is materially stronger than the applicable expected, engineered, historical, or configured value.

symptom_types.name: RSL_DISCREPANCY
symptom_types.description: Two or more RSL values that are expected to reasonably correspond differ materially.

symptom_types.name: MAIN_DIVERSITY_RSL_IMBALANCE
symptom_types.description: Main and Diversity receive levels differ materially beyond the applicable expected relationship.

symptom_types.name: LOCAL_REMOTE_RSL_IMBALANCE
symptom_types.description: Corresponding receive levels at opposite microwave endpoints differ materially beyond expected behavior.

symptom_types.name: UNSTABLE_RSL
symptom_types.description: Received Signal Level varies materially over time without an expected operational explanation.

symptom_types.name: NO_RSL
symptom_types.description: Expected receive signal is absent, undetectable, or reported below the usable receiver condition.

symptom_types.name: LOW_SNR
symptom_types.description: Signal-to-noise ratio is below the applicable expected or acceptable condition.

symptom_types.name: LOW_SINR
symptom_types.description: Signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio is below the applicable expected or acceptable condition.

symptom_types.name: LOW_XPD
symptom_types.description: Measured cross-polarization discrimination is below the applicable requirement or expected condition.

symptom_types.name: LOW_FADE_MARGIN
symptom_types.description: Available receive margin above the applicable receiver threshold is lower than required or engineered.

symptom_types.name: LINK_DOWN
symptom_types.description: Microwave link is not operational or traffic-bearing when operation is expected.

symptom_types.name: LINK_FLAPPING
symptom_types.description: Link repeatedly transitions between operational and non-operational states.

symptom_types.name: ONE_WAY_LINK
symptom_types.description: Communication or expected RF/system behavior is present in one direction but absent or materially degraded in the opposite direction.

symptom_types.name: PARTIAL_LINK_OPERATION
symptom_types.description: A microwave system is operational only in part, such as one radio, carrier, polarization, or path functioning while another is not.

symptom_types.name: MAIN_PATH_DOWN
symptom_types.description: The designated Main RF or radio path is unavailable while other system elements may remain operational.

symptom_types.name: DIVERSITY_PATH_DOWN
symptom_types.description: The designated Diversity RF or radio path is unavailable while other system elements may remain operational.

symptom_types.name: HIGH_BER
symptom_types.description: Bit Error Rate exceeds the applicable acceptable threshold or expected operating condition.

symptom_types.name: HIGH_PACKET_ERROR_RATE
symptom_types.description: Packet Error Rate exceeds the applicable acceptable threshold.

symptom_types.name: PACKET_LOSS
symptom_types.description: Observed packet loss exceeds the applicable expected or acceptable condition.

symptom_types.name: LOW_THROUGHPUT
symptom_types.description: Measured traffic throughput is materially below the expected, configured, or engineered capability.

symptom_types.name: LOW_CAPACITY
symptom_types.description: Available or reported microwave capacity is materially below the expected or configured condition.

symptom_types.name: LOW_MODULATION
symptom_types.description: Current modulation state is below the expected or normally sustainable modulation level.

symptom_types.name: MODULATION_FLAPPING
symptom_types.description: Adaptive modulation repeatedly transitions between materially different operating states.

symptom_types.name: HIGH_ERRORED_SECONDS
symptom_types.description: Errored Seconds exceed the applicable expected or acceptable condition.

symptom_types.name: HIGH_SEVERELY_ERRORED_SECONDS
symptom_types.description: Severely Errored Seconds exceed the applicable expected or acceptable condition.

symptom_types.name: HIGH_UNAVAILABLE_SECONDS
symptom_types.description: Unavailable Seconds exceed the applicable expected or acceptable condition.

symptom_types.name: HIGH_LATENCY
symptom_types.description: Measured latency exceeds the applicable expected or acceptable threshold.

symptom_types.name: HIGH_JITTER
symptom_types.description: Measured packet-delay variation exceeds the applicable expected or acceptable threshold.

symptom_types.name: FREQUENCY_MISMATCH
symptom_types.description: Observed or reported frequency values that should correspond do not match.

symptom_types.name: CHANNEL_BANDWIDTH_MISMATCH
symptom_types.description: Observed or reported channel bandwidth values that should correspond do not match.

symptom_types.name: TX_POWER_DISCREPANCY
symptom_types.description: Actual, reported, configured, expected, or endpoint transmit-power values differ materially.

symptom_types.name: CONFIGURATION_MISMATCH
symptom_types.description: Two configuration states that are expected to correspond are materially inconsistent.

symptom_types.name: DESIGN_CONFIGURATION_MISMATCH
symptom_types.description: Configured system state differs materially from the applicable engineering design.

symptom_types.name: ACTIVE_RADIO_ALARM
symptom_types.description: One or more radio-related alarms are active.

symptom_types.name: ACTIVE_RF_ALARM
symptom_types.description: One or more RF-related alarms are active.

symptom_types.name: ACTIVE_CONFIGURATION_ALARM
symptom_types.description: One or more alarms indicate a configuration inconsistency, invalid state, or configuration-related problem.

symptom_types.name: ACTIVE_HARDWARE_ALARM
symptom_types.description: One or more alarms indicate hardware abnormality or failure.

symptom_types.name: ACTIVE_POWER_ALARM
symptom_types.description: One or more alarms indicate abnormal equipment power conditions.

symptom_types.name: NO_POWER
symptom_types.description: Equipment expected to be powered is not receiving or reporting usable power.

symptom_types.name: LOW_VOLTAGE
symptom_types.description: Measured equipment supply voltage is below the applicable expected or acceptable range.

symptom_types.name: UNSTABLE_POWER
symptom_types.description: Equipment supply power or voltage varies materially or intermittently outside expected behavior.

symptom_types.name: VISIBLE_COMPONENT_DAMAGE
symptom_types.description: Physical inspection reveals visible damage to equipment or an RF-chain component.

symptom_types.name: VISIBLE_WATER_INGRESS
symptom_types.description: Physical inspection reveals water, moisture, corrosion, or evidence of moisture intrusion.

symptom_types.name: LOOSE_CONNECTION_OBSERVED
symptom_types.description: Physical inspection reveals a connection that is loose, unseated, improperly retained, or otherwise mechanically suspect.

symptom_types.name: INCORRECT_COMPONENT_OBSERVED
symptom_types.description: Physical inspection indicates that an installed component differs from the applicable design or required hardware.

symptom_types.name: LOS_OBSTRUCTION_OBSERVED
symptom_types.description: A physical obstruction is observed within or near the microwave propagation path.

symptom_types.name: FRESNEL_CLEARANCE_DEFICIENCY
symptom_types.description: Observed or calculated Fresnel-zone clearance is below the applicable requirement.

symptom_types.name: AZIMUTH_DISCREPANCY
symptom_types.description: Observed antenna azimuth differs materially from the applicable design azimuth.

symptom_types.name: ELEVATION_DISCREPANCY
symptom_types.description: Observed antenna elevation angle differs materially from the applicable design.

symptom_types.name: ANTENNA_HEIGHT_DISCREPANCY
symptom_types.description: Observed installed antenna height differs materially from the applicable engineering design.

symptom_types.name: WEATHER_CORRELATED_DEGRADATION
symptom_types.description: Technical degradation is observed to correlate with changing weather conditions without independently establishing the specific environmental cause.

symptom_types.name: RAIN_CORRELATED_RSL_DEGRADATION
symptom_types.description: RSL degradation is observed during precipitation and materially changes with precipitation conditions.

symptom_types.name: WIND_CORRELATED_RSL_VARIATION
symptom_types.description: RSL variation is observed to correlate with wind conditions.

symptom_types.name: TEMPERATURE_CORRELATED_FAILURE
symptom_types.description: Failure or degradation is observed to correlate with equipment or ambient temperature.

symptom_types.name: REFERENCE_DATA_CONFLICT
symptom_types.description: Two or more authoritative or operational reference sources contain materially conflicting technical information.

symptom_types.name: SITE_INFORMATION_MISMATCH
symptom_types.description: Observed site, path, endpoint, configuration, or equipment information does not correspond with the expected site information.

symptom_types.name: UNCLASSIFIED_ABNORMAL_CONDITION
symptom_types.description: An abnormal condition has been reported or observed but cannot yet be mapped confidently to a more specific canonical symptom.

semantic_rules.rule: A symptom describes an observed or reported condition and shall not independently establish the underlying failure mode or root cause.
ARIA shall preserve the distinction between a raw observation, a derived symptom, a hypothesis, and a confirmed diagnosis.
Multiple symptoms may coexist within a single case and may jointly provide substantially more diagnostic information than any symptom evaluated independently.

A discrepancy symptom requires an explicit comparison basis. ARIA shall preserve what was compared, such as Main versus Diversity, Local versus Remote, Actual versus Expected, or Actual versus Design.
Manufacturer terminology and technician slang shall map to canonical symptoms through aliases or graph relationships rather than creating duplicate symptom classes.
A symptom may increase or decrease the probability of multiple competing hypotheses and shall not be treated as uniquely identifying a root cause unless validated evidence supports that conclusion.
Correlated observations such as weather-correlated degradation describe correlation only. Correlation shall not be promoted to causation without sufficient supporting evidence.
Historical diagnostic probabilities associated with symptoms belong to the Experience Ledger and reasoning layers and shall not be encoded as fixed probabilities in this registry.
ARIA should prefer the most specific symptom supported by evidence while retaining broader symptoms when they remain independently useful for reasoning.
UNCLASSIFIED_ABNORMAL_CONDITION shall be used only when available information cannot yet support a more specific canonical symptom.
